sources.name: Claude API release notes
sources.why: The source of truth for Claude API changes: models, parameters, prices, deprecations. Shows launches before the news page does.

sources.name: OpenAI API changelog
sources.why: Every OpenAI API change, dated and tagged with the model or endpoint it touches.

sources.name: Gemini API changelog
sources.why: Gemini has the most usable free API tier, so its model and access changes matter on a zero budget.

sources.name: Claude Code releases
sources.why: New flags, hooks and agent features in the tool you use daily. About 6 releases a week, mostly fixes.

sources.name: Ollama releases
sources.why: What changed in the thing that runs models on your Mac.

sources.name: LangGraph releases
sources.why: Changes to the framework you're learning. Mostly patch releases; triage drops those.

sources.name: Model Context Protocol blog
sources.why: Changes to the MCP spec, which every agent tool (Claude Code included) now speaks.

sources.name: claude.dev
sources.why: Anthropic's blog for builders, mostly by the Claude Code team. Where their hands-on writing lives now.

sources.name: OpenAI News
sources.why: OpenAI launches and research land here first. Noisy (~17 posts a week), so customer stories are dropped up front.

sources.name: Google DeepMind blog
sources.why: Gemini and Gemma launches and DeepMind research, from the source.

sources.name: Hugging Face blog
sources.why: Open-model releases and practical guides from the hub everything open is hosted on.

sources.name: Hugging Face trending models
sources.why: New open-weight models people are actually downloading, with sizes, so you can tell if one fits in 24 GB.

sources.name: OpenRouter new models
sources.why: Every new model from every lab (Chinese labs included) with its price, context window and any free route.

sources.name: r/LocalLLaMA
sources.why: Where 'does it run on a 24 GB Mac?' gets answered within hours of a release.

sources.name: Ollama blog
sources.why: New models and features for running locally on Apple Silicon.

sources.name: Hugging Face Papers
sources.why: Research papers ranked by builders' upvotes: the top handful instead of 500 a day.

sources.name: Ahead of AI (Sebastian Raschka)
sources.why: Explains model architecture at the depth interviews probe: attention variants, reasoning, training.

sources.name: Interconnects (Nathan Lambert)
sources.why: Open models and post-training, by someone who trains models for a living.

sources.name: Deep (Learning) Focus
sources.why: Long, clear explainers of one LLM research topic at a time.

sources.name: Lil'Log (Lilian Weng)
sources.why: Rare posts, each a definitive survey of one topic. Worth knowing the moment one appears.

sources.name: Andrej Karpathy
sources.why: Low volume, high signal. His blog is the live outlet now; the YouTube channel has been quiet since Feb 2025.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis
sources.why: Independent speed, price and quality numbers for each notable launch: the check on a vendor's own chart.

sources.name: Simon Willison
sources.why: Ships code against every model he writes about, so he tells you whether a release changes what you can build.

sources.name: Latent Space
sources.why: swyx's daily AINews recap plus practitioner interviews on agents and production systems.

sources.name: Hamel Husain
sources.why: Evals, by the person who taught them to 700+ engineers. Evals are the skill that sets you apart.

sources.name: Eugene Yan
sources.why: A data scientist turned AI engineer: the move you're making, written up as it happens.

sources.name: AI Engineer (YouTube)
sources.why: Conference talks by people running AI in production, failure modes included.

sources.name: Dave Ebbelaar (YouTube)
sources.why: Applied, watchable AI engineering. One of the two best fits from your video roadmap.

sources.name: Neural Breakdown with AVB (YouTube)
sources.why: Clear visual explainers of ML ideas. The other best fit from your video roadmap.

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.why: AI stories engineers upvoted past 50 points, plus any story past 300 (product names like 'Pi 1.0' hide AI).

sources.name: GitHub Trending (today)
sources.why: The repos 'ranked #1 on GitHub' in reels, read from GitHub itself, with stars gained today so you can tell viral from established.

sources.name: GitHub Trending (this week)
sources.why: Catches the ones that peaked on a day you didn't pull. A repo in both lists shows up once.

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
sources.why: Careful reporting for the headline layer: policy, lawsuits and launches, with less hype than most.
